sections.h2: What should a home seller know about Colorado as a whole?
sections.html:
Colorado is a large, mountain-and-plains state where the rules for selling a house are mostly set by the state and carried out county by county. The state covers 104,185 square miles, ranks 8th in area and had 6,012,561 residents in 2025, according to the state's Wikipedia entry.

Denver is the capital and the largest city. Colorado Springs is the second most populous city. The state was admitted to the Union on August 1, 1876, as the 38th state.

Wikipedia lists a median household income of $92,900 for 2023 and the economy as government and defense, mining, agriculture, tourism and manufacturing. For a seller, that mix means very different local markets under one set of state rules.

sections.h2: How is Colorado divided into regions?
sections.html:
Most of the population lives along the Front Range, east of the Rockies. Wikipedia names Denver, Boulder, Fort Collins, Loveland, Castle Rock, Colorado Springs, Pueblo and Greeley among the Front Range cities, along with towns in between.

West of the mountains is the Western Slope, where the larger population centers are Grand Junction, Durango and Montrose. About half of the state is flat or rolling land, and the Eastern Plains sit between roughly 3,350 and 7,500 feet.

The three areas behave differently for a seller:

  • Front Range. The corridor that includes Denver and Colorado Springs.
  • Western Slope. The side of the Rockies where Grand Junction, Durango and Montrose sit.
  • Eastern Plains. Mostly farmland and rangeland, with small farming villages and towns.

The plains receive about 15 to 25 inches of precipitation a year and grow corn, wheat, hay, soybeans and oats.

sections.h2: How many counties does Colorado have, and why does it matter?
sections.html:
Colorado has 64 counties, and the county is the key local unit of government because the state has no civil townships or other minor civil divisions. Two of them, Denver and Broomfield, are consolidated city and county governments.

That structure shapes almost every step of a sale. The county clerk and recorder records the deed and collects a state documentary fee. The county treasurer collects property tax. The sheriff schedules removals after an eviction judgment.

El Paso County is the largest by population. Denver and Broomfield have only one local government to deal with, since the city and county are the same body. In the other 62 counties, cities and towns sit inside a county, so a seller may deal with both.

Courts follow a separate map. Colorado has 23 judicial districts, each with a district court and a county court of limited jurisdiction, plus water courts in seven divisions for water rights.

sections.h2: What does the state charge when a deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Colorado imposes a documentary fee on deeds. C.R.S. 39-13-102 sets it at one cent for each $100 of consideration, collected by the county clerk and recorder in addition to the ordinary recording fee.

The first rules to know:

  • No fee applies when there is no consideration, or when the total is $500 or less.
  • The person offering the deed for recording pays.
  • If a single sale covers land in more than one county, each clerk collects a share in proportion to the value in that county.
  • For a residential sale, the consideration is generally the amount listed on the deed, unless the deed lists nothing or $500 or less and a declaration sets the sales price.
  • A property is treated as residential for this fee unless the deed states otherwise.

Because the fee is statewide and based only on price, it is the same arithmetic in Denver as it is in a small plains county.

sections.h2: How is property tax paid in Colorado?
sections.html:
Colorado property tax is paid to the county treasurer, in full or in two installments. Under C.R.S. 39-10-104.5, the first half is due the last day of February and the second half by June 15. Paying the full amount by April 30 avoids interest.

Payment choiceDue date
Two halvesLast day of February, then June 15
One paymentOn or before April 30
Total under $25In full by April 30

Late payments accrue delinquent interest at one percent per month. The statute also says payment counts as received on the postmark date, with a five-day grace rule for mail that has no postmark.

The county treasurer is the best place to confirm a balance before closing, because a late installment adds interest every month.

sections.h2: What other statewide rules affect a Colorado sale?
sections.html:
Three state topics come up for sellers again and again: homestead protection, rented houses and estate sales.

  • Homestead. The creditor exemption for an occupied home is $250,000, or $350,000 for an elderly or disabled owner, spouse or dependent, under C.R.S. 38-41-201.
  • Evictions. The standard residential notice is ten days, and a no-fault notice because the owner wants to sell needs at least 90 days.
  • Inherited property. A personal representative can sell, and a heir who refuses to leave after the sale can be removed under the eviction statute.

Each of those has its own page on this site, with the statute and the court forms. This page is the overview, and the city and county pages below it cover local details.

The state's judicial branch publishes the court forms for evictions, and the legislature's site hosts the statutes. Neither replaces advice from a Colorado attorney for a live dispute.

sections.h2: Why do Colorado city markets differ so much?
sections.html:
Terrain, economy and county structure change how a sale works from one Colorado city to the next. A suburb on the Front Range has a different buyer pool than a Western Slope town, and a plains farm town has a different one again.

Wikipedia calls Colorado's economy a mix of government and defense, mining, agriculture, tourism and manufacturing, and notes that the state expects climate change to affect agriculture, forestry and tourism. Those industries sit in different parts of the state, so local demand varies.

What stays the same is the process. A seller records a deed with the county, pays the documentary fee, clears property tax with the county treasurer and follows state rules for any tenant. Our city and county guides apply those steps to a specific place.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in Colorado?
sections.html:
A cash sale uses the same recorded deed, tax and fee steps as any other Colorado sale, without a lender's approval process in the middle. The seller and buyer sign a contract, a title company clears the title, and the deed is recorded with the county clerk and recorder.

Before you call anyone, gather the basics:

  1. The property address and county.
  2. Any lease, notice or court papers if the house is rented.
  3. The latest property tax statement.
  4. Any lien, judgment or mortgage payoff information.

With those four items, a buyer can give you a realistic read on timing. We buy houses in Colorado as is, and we are happy to look at your situation with you.

faqs.q: How many counties are in Colorado?
faqs.a: Colorado has 64 counties. Denver and Broomfield are consolidated city and county governments, and El Paso is the largest county.

faqs.q: What is the Colorado documentary fee on a house sale?
faqs.a: One cent for each $100 of consideration, paid by the person offering the deed for recording. No fee applies when consideration is $500 or less.

faqs.q: When are Colorado property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due the last day of February and the second half by June 15. The full amount can be paid by April 30 without interest.

faqs.q: What is the interest on late Colorado property taxes?
faqs.a: One percent per month, counted by whole months, under C.R.S. 39-10-104.5.

faqs.q: Where does a Colorado eviction case get filed?
faqs.a: In the county where the property is located. Colorado has 23 judicial districts, each with a district court and a county court.

faqs.q: How much does the Colorado homestead exemption protect?
faqs.a: $250,000 for an owner-occupied home and $350,000 for an elderly or disabled owner, spouse or dependent.

faqs.q: Which Colorado cities are on the Front Range?
faqs.a: Wikipedia lists Denver, Boulder, Fort Collins, Loveland, Castle Rock, Colorado Springs, Pueblo and Greeley among them.
